investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never left the Pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity (all VM slots consumed or at limit), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no vmIdPresent or remoteState values, causing a complete contract gap for all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata-peerpods node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: the 4 non-kata nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity/selector, meaning the effective scheduling domain is only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity reduced, new pods would immediately be unschedulable.

Tertiary — kata-peerpods resource quota or limit range set too low for the current workload: a cluster-level or namespace-level ResourceQuota on kata.peerpods.io/vm may cap total allocatable VMs below current demand.

Lower confidence — node pool not scaled out to meet demand: the cluster autoscaler may not be configured to add kata-peerpods nodes, or scale-out was blocked, leaving only 2 nodes permanently available for this resource type.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-22T00:55–01:00Z with identical Kubernetes scheduler messages reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the requested pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never returned an agent, and the remote-agent-state check produced zero evidence — all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) are missing.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted by the eval runner (and by extension any real remote-agent creation request routed through the same cluster) is stuck Unschedulable. The eval fails because createAgent never completes, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is ever written, violating the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 264.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the cluster has consumed all available peer-pod VM slots on the only nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving no schedulable capacity. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes never match the pod's affinity rules, meaning the effective scheduling pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are undersized for the expected VM concurrency, any burst of remote-agent creation will exhaust capacity (evidence: failed-check.message '4 node(s) didn't match Pod\'s node affinity/selector').

Tertiary — leaked or zombie peer-pod VMs holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: previously created remote agents that were not cleaned up may be holding VM resource allocations, preventing new pods from scheduling (evidence: all three sibling checks failed in sequence within the same ~5-minute window, suggesting slots were not released between runs).

Lower confidence — eval runner cleanup (withCleanup) not releasing VM resources from a prior run: if a previous eval run crashed before cleanup, its VM slot may still be allocated (evidence: source-context run-status-probes.mjs:1903 shows withCleanup wrapping the probe, but no evidence of prior run history is available — verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the underlying VM pod never left the Pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient allocatable capacity (all VM slots consumed or at limit), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no vmIdPresent or remoteState values, causing a complete contract gap for all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm/kata-peerpods node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=147647 (~147s), which exceeds the pod-stuck threshold reported in the message (143s) and is well below the warningLatencyMs=240000 threshold, confirming the check failed on scheduling timeout rather than a latency breach.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all allocatable VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, indicating no lower-priority pods are evictable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or node pool shrinkage: the 4 non-kata nodes are excluded by the pod's affinity/selector, meaning the effective scheduling domain is only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently cordoned, drained, or had their kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity reduced, new pods would immediately be unschedulable.

Tertiary — kata-peerpods resource quota or limit range set too low for the current workload: a cluster-level or namespace-level ResourceQuota on kata.peerpods.io/vm may cap total allocatable VMs below current demand.

Lower confidence — node pool not scaled out to meet demand: the cluster autoscaler may not be configured to add kata-peerpods nodes, or scale-out was blocked, leaving only 2 nodes permanently available for this resource type.

investigations.title: Remote Agent VM Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-22T00:55–01:00Z because every pod submitted to the production Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No agent VM was ever provisioned, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place remote-agent pods because the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is exhausted across the two eligible nodes (0/2 available) and the other four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. This is a cluster-capacity or resource-quota constraint in the production-api runtime environment, not an application code defect. Because no pod ever started, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) never returned, the probe timed out after ~148 s, and zero evidence was collected against the expected-output contract.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message and asserts message containsIgnoreCase 'hello from aura' — none of these can be satisfied if the pod never starts.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: all existing remote-agent VM slots are occupied by running or leaked pods, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets a node label or taint that only two nodes satisfy, and those two nodes are also the only ones with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. If the selector was recently narrowed or node labels changed, capacity would appear to drop to zero even if physical VMs are available.

Tertiary — resource quota or LimitRange at the namespace level capping kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations below the number of concurrent eval pods, causing the scheduler to report Insufficient even when node-level capacity exists.

Quaternary — a previous eval run's cleanup did not release the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource (e.g., a leaked pod or stuck terminating pod), consuming the available slots and starving subsequent runs. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916), but if a prior run crashed before cleanup, slots may remain held.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is zero (i.e., the nodes were never configured with this resource), the cause would be a misconfiguration or missing device plugin rather than exhaustion.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots but the scheduler still reports Insufficient, the cause would be a resource quota or LimitRange at the namespace level, not node-level exhaustion.

If the node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec was recently changed to target only the two kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes and those nodes are otherwise healthy with free capacity, the cause would be a selector change rather than capacity exhaustion.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after freeing one VM slot succeeds and produces all five required evidence fields, that would confirm capacity exhaustion as the sole cause and rule out application-level regressions.
If local-agent checks (local-agent-create, local-agent-runtime) are also failing with scheduling errors, the problem may be broader than the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool alone.
